title: CLARITY Act Update for XRP Army: Lummis and Warren Clash Publicly. Here’s why
body: The Senate’s ongoing debate over the CLARITY Act has taken a sharper turn. Senator Cynthia Lummis and Senator Elizabeth Warren are now trading public accusations over the bill’s ethics provision, with Warren’s staff releasing a formal analysis and Lummis responding directly. CoinDesk reported the exchange on X, capturing one of the most visible flashpoints in a months-long negotiation standoff. LATEST: @SenLummis and @SenWarren clash publicly over the CLARITY Act's ethics provision. Warren's staff calls it "riddled with loopholes" that would let Trump keep earning from crypto, Lummis fires back calling the analysis dishonest. pic.twitter.com/cPcvW1pelL — CoinDesk (@CoinDesk) August 1, 2026 What Warren’s Staff Calls It The dispute centers on ethics language that Republican negotiators released on July 22 . Warren’s minority staff on the Senate Banking Committee reviewed the text and concluded it was “riddled with major loopholes.” Their analysis argued the provisions would not prevent President Trump from continuing to profit from his cryptocurrency ventures. Trump earned more than $1.4 billion from crypto in 2025 alone, according to financial disclosures. His ventures include the $TRUMP memecoin and World Liberty Financial. Warren’s staff argued that even if the provisions technically applied to his profits, enforcement would fall to a Justice Department of his own choosing. This ethics debate has held up the bill for weeks . Lummis Responds Lummis rejected the Democratic analysis. She accused Warren of prioritizing opposition to Trump over protections for consumers, writing that Warren “hates President Trump so much that she’d rather have no rules of the road for the digital asset industry.” She defended the ethics language on three specific points and described Warren’s fact sheet as dishonest. Lummis has consistently argued the goal of the provision is to build durable ethics standards across all three branches of government, not to target a single officeholder. We are on X, follow us to connect with us :- @TimesTabloid1 — TimesTabloid (@TimesTabloid1) June 15, 2025 The Bill’s Current Position The Senate Banking Committee advanced the CLARITY Act in May. Since then, the ethics question has stalled the bill on the Senate floor. A bipartisan counterproposal from Senators Thom Tillis and Ruben Gallego arrived at the White House Thursday. It would give state attorneys general the power to sue the DOJ if it fails to enforce ethics laws against federal officials. A previous White House offer failed to win enough Democratic support. Senate Majority Leader John Thune also previously pledged a floor vote before the August 8 recess. Lummis has closed the door on further negotiation . “I think we just vote and let the chips fall where they may,” she said. The White House’s response to the Tillis-Gallego proposal will determine whether a vote happens before recess. title: Teleprompter Operator Accused in Kalshi Betting Case Is No Longer a Federal Employee
body: White House teleprompter operator Gabriel Perez is no longer employed by the federal government after being placed on unpaid leave over allegations that he used insider knowledge to bet on President Donald Trump’s speeches, according to another official. Speaking on condition of anonymity, the official said that Perez had left his government job but did not say whether he resigned or was fired. Inside the Allegations The White House had suspended Perez earlier this month following an ABC News report that alleged he made more than $100,000 through bets on the online prediction market Kalshi. The report said the wagers were based on advance knowledge of what Trump would say during major speeches, including the State of the Union address earlier this year. The allegations drew a sharp response from the White House. Press secretary Karoline Leavitt described the reported insider trading as “deeply unfortunate and, frankly, a disgrace.” Kalshi also responded after the report was published . Robert Denault, the company’s lawyer and head of enforcement, said in a post on X that its surveillance team detected the trades, investigated them, and referred the matter to the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC). Denault’s statement did not identify Perez by name. Legal Battles Kalshi has faced legal hurdles this year in Massachusetts, Michigan, Nevada, and Washington. At the same time, it has also tightened its own rules. In April, the prediction market suspended three political candidates for betting on elections they were contesting after determining that the trades amounted to political insider trading under its CFTC-approved rules. An insider trading case on Polymarket also surfaced that same month. Federal prosecutors charged US soldier Gannon Ken Van Dyke with allegedly betting on whether former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro would be removed from power. Authorities said Van Dyke, who worked on the operation targeting Maduro, made about $400,000 from the trades. The legal battle over prediction markets has also taken a new turn. This week, a federal judge temporarily blocked Minnesota from enforcing a new law that would have banned prediction markets in the state. The ruling gave a temporary win to Kalshi, Polymarket, and the CFTC as the case moves forward. Judge Katherine Menendez said the law is likely preempted by the federal Commodity Exchange Act because many event contracts may qualify as federally regulated swaps. The law, signed by Governor Tim Walz in May, was set to take effect on Saturday. The judge said the injunction could later be narrowed if needed.
